questions.question: Describe segregation before 1948 and explain why the National Party won the 1948 election.
questions.expected_answer: Before 1948: colonial conquest; Union 1910 gave whites power (limited Cape franchise); SANNC/ANC 1912; Natives Land Act 1913 (7%), Trust and Land Act 1936 (13%); Natives (Urban Areas) Act 1923; pass laws; Cape African voters removed 1936; job reservation. 1948: wartime urbanisation and informal settlements, 1946 mine strike; Fagan vs Sauer Commission; swart gevaar; Afrikaner nationalism (South African War memories, poor whites, Broederbond); NP + Afrikaner Party 79 seats vs UP + Labour 71, despite fewer votes, due to weighted rural constituencies; Malan PM; NP ruled until 1994. Aims: white control, protect white jobs, control black labour, divide opposition.

questions.question: Outline the main apartheid laws, grouped by what they controlled.
questions.expected_answer: Classification: Population Registration Act 1950. Relationships: Prohibition of Mixed Marriages Act 1949, Immorality Amendment Act 1950. Residence: Group Areas Act 1950 (forced removals). Movement: Natives (Abolition of Passes and Co-ordination of Documents) Act 1952 (reference book, arrests). Facilities: Reservation of Separate Amenities Act 1953 (need not be equal). Education: Bantu Education Act 1953 (Verwoerd), Extension of University Education Act 1959. Political/opposition: Suppression of Communism Act 1950, Bantu Authorities Act 1951, Separate Representation of Voters Act 1951 (achieved 1956), Promotion of Bantu Self-Government Act 1959.

questions.question: Distinguish petty and grand apartheid and describe the effects of apartheid laws.
questions.expected_answer: Petty: everyday segregation of facilities, signs, separate transport, beaches, entrances, mixed marriage bans; humiliating. Grand: separation of land and political rights; Verwoerd (PM 1958) homelands/bantustans, black people as citizens of homelands, forced removals of millions. Effects: families split (classification, migrant labour), communities destroyed, inferior education, no vote, banning, imprisonment; resistance from the start; some white opposition (UP, Liberal, Progressive Parties, Black Sash), but most white voters supported NP.
